title: Several Circles
spot: Find a circle with a tiny black dot in the middle, like an eye. How many can you count?
story: Kandinsky thought colours worked like music — he even named many paintings "Compositions." Does this one look loud or quiet to you?

title: Discomedusae (Art Forms in Nature, plate 8)
spot: This jellyfish is drawn from below and from the side. Follow one long frilly arm from top to bottom.
story: Haeckel was a scientist who drew the sea creatures he studied, many under a microscope. He named thousands of new species.

title: Composition 8
spot: Find the big black circle, a checkerboard and something that looks like a ladder.
story: Kandinsky painted this while teaching at the Bauhaus, a famous German art and design school. It's one of his calmest, most geometric paintings.

title: Banana Flower and Fruit
place: Metamorphosis of the Insects of Surinam
spot: Find the caterpillar and the moth. Could they be the same animal at different ages?
story: In 1699, at age 52, Merian sailed to South America to study insects and how they change — something almost no woman did back then.

title: Castle and Sun
spot: Count the triangles. Can you find the sun?
story: Klee built this whole castle from simple shapes, like building blocks. He was also a very good violin player.

title: Plum Park in Kameido
place: One Hundred Famous Views of Edo
spot: Which branch is closest to you? Find the people behind the fence.
story: Hiroshige zoomed in on one branch like a photographer. Van Gogh loved this print so much he painted his own copy.

title: Composition II in Red, Blue, and Yellow
spot: Which colour has the biggest box? How many rectangles can you count?
story: Mondrian used only straight lines, black, white, grey and three main colours. He wanted the simplest possible picture to feel perfectly balanced.

title: Forest, British Columbia
spot: Find the path that leads deep into the forest. Where do you think it goes?
story: Carr painted the giant trees of the BC coast so they seem to sway and breathe. She was also a writer and won a Governor General's Award.

title: Suprematist Composition: Airplane Flying
spot: Do these shapes look like an airplane to you? Which way is it flying?
story: Malevich wanted paintings with no objects at all — just pure shapes and colour. He called it Suprematism.

title: Trochilidae (Art Forms in Nature)
spot: How many hummingbirds can you count? Which one has the longest tail?
story: Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backwards. Their hearts can beat more than 1,000 times a minute.

title: The Ten Largest, No. 7, Adulthood
spot: Find spirals, flowers and letters hiding in the swirls.
story: Af Klint painted abstract art years before most famous abstract painters — and asked that it not be shown until 20 years after her death.

title: Silver Sun
spot: Is that a sun, an eye, or something else? What do you see?
story: Dove is often called America's first abstract painter. He tried to paint how nature feels, not just how it looks.

title: Simultaneous Contrasts: Sun and Moon
spot: Where is the sun, and where is the moon?
story: Delaunay was fascinated by how colours seem to change when they sit right next to each other. Try covering half the painting with your hand.

title: North Shore, Lake Superior
spot: What does the tree stump remind you of? Follow the light from the sky.
story: Harris, from Brantford, Ontario, was a founder of the Group of Seven. Later in life his paintings became completely abstract.

title: Senecio
spot: Which eyebrow is raised? What is this face feeling?
story: Klee described drawing as taking a line for a walk. This whole face is built from a circle, squares and triangles.

title: Ascending Forms
spot: Find the black circles stacked like a tower. What's at the very top?
story: In 1927 Brooker showed abstract paintings at the Arts and Letters Club in Toronto — the first abstract art exhibition by a Canadian artist.

title: Yellow-Red-Blue
spot: Find a yellow shape, a red one and a blue one. Which one feels the loudest?
story: Kandinsky believed yellow felt warm and bright, and blue felt calm and deep. Do you agree?

title: Brooklyn Bridge
spot: Find the bridge cables, the arches and the city lights.
story: Stella came to New York from Italy and saw the Brooklyn Bridge as a great cathedral made of steel.

title: Squares with Concentric Circles
spot: Find two squares that use the same colours. Which circle is the smallest?
story: Kandinsky made this as a colour study, testing which colours sing together. It turned into one of his best-loved pictures.

title: On White II
spot: Find the checkerboards, the dice and the black lines shooting across.
story: Kandinsky painted this while teaching at the Bauhaus. He said a white background is like a great silence, full of possibilities.

title: Fish Magic
spot: Find the clock, a flower and as many fish as you can.
story: Klee glued a square of thin cloth onto the middle of this painting. Can you spot its edges?

title: Red Balloon
spot: Find the red balloon. What is it floating over?
story: Klee and Kandinsky both taught at the Bauhaus. For years they lived next door to each other.

title: The Yellow Cow
spot: Is the cow jumping, dancing or running? Find the blue mountains.
story: Marc gave colours feelings. To him yellow meant gentle and cheerful, which is why this cow is anything but brown.

title: Lady in a Green Jacket
spot: Count the people. Who is wearing green? Find the lake behind them.
story: Macke loved bright colours and people strolling in parks. He was killed early in World War I, at just 27.

title: Windows Open Simultaneously
spot: Can you find the green Eiffel Tower hiding among the coloured panes?
story: Delaunay painted light pouring through a window as if it were broken into coloured pieces, like looking through a prism.

title: Painterly Architectonic
spot: Which shape is on top? Which one is at the very back?
story: Popova was a leader of the Russian avant-garde. Later she designed fabrics and stage sets using the same bold shapes.

title: Green Stripe
spot: Are the stripe's edges sharp or soft? Does it look like it's glowing?
story: Rozanova painted a single stripe decades before famous American painters did the same. She died the next year, at just 32.

title: Beat the Whites with the Red Wedge
spot: Find the red wedge and the white circle. Which one seems to be winning?
story: A poster from the Russian Civil War: the red wedge stood for the "Reds" and the white circle for the "Whites." Lissitzky told a story with only shapes.

title: The Cow
spot: Can you find the cow? Hint: it has turned into rectangles.
story: Van Doesburg drew a cow again and again, simplifying each time until only coloured blocks were left. With Mondrian he started the De Stijl movement.

title: I Saw the Figure 5 in Gold
spot: How many 5s can you find? Look for the names BILL and CARLO too.
story: It's a picture of a poem: Demuth's friend William Carlos Williams wrote about a red fire truck numbered 5 racing through the rainy city.

title: Portrait of a German Officer
spot: Find the letters K v F and the number 24.
story: There's no face, but it's a portrait. Hartley made it for his friend Karl von Freyburg, killed in World War I at age 24.

title: Portrait of Félix Fénéon
spot: What is Fénéon holding out? Find the stars behind him.
story: Signac painted it all with tiny dots of pure colour. Fénéon was an art critic who gave this dotty style its name: Neo-Impressionism.

title: The Cyclops
spot: Find the giant's one eye, then the person sleeping on the hillside.
story: In a Greek myth, the cyclops Polyphemus falls in love with the sea nymph Galatea. Redon makes him shy, just peeking over the hill.

title: The Swan, No. 17
spot: Which half is light and which is dark? Find black, white, yellow and blue.
story: Af Klint's Swan series starts with a black swan and a white swan. Painting by painting, they turn into pure shapes about opposites.

title: Snow at Zōjō-ji
spot: Find the person with the umbrella. Is the snow still falling?
story: Hasui made more than 600 prints of Japanese landscapes. Japan later named him a Living National Treasure.

title: Crow and Blossom
spot: Find the crow's eye. How many blossoms are open?
story: Koson made hundreds of bird-and-flower prints, many of them sold to collectors in Europe and America.

title: Kirifuri Waterfall
place: A Tour of the Waterfalls of the Provinces
spot: Find the tiny travellers looking up at the falls.
story: This is by the artist of the famous Great Wave. He drew the water like fingers or roots reaching down the mountain.

title: Actiniae (sea anemones)
spot: These look like flowers, but they're animals! Find one with tentacles like spaghetti.
story: Sea anemones catch food with stinging tentacles. Clownfish are protected from the stings, so they live safely inside them.

title: Totem and Forest
spot: Find the carved faces on the pole. How tall do you think it is?
story: Carr spent years visiting First Nations villages along the BC coast, painting their carved poles among the giant trees.

title: The West Wind
spot: Which way is the wind blowing? How can you tell?
story: Thomson painted the lakes of Algonquin Park, a few hours north of Toronto. You can see this one in person at the AGO.

title: Nude Descending a Staircase, No. 2
spot: Find the figure walking down the stairs. How many times can you see it?
story: It shows movement like a stack of photos taken in a row. At a 1913 show in New York, one critic called it "an explosion in a shingle factory."
